questions.question: Which of bundles 1–4 should get a backlog item?

options.label: 1 Fixture completeness (Recommended)
options.description: BK, effort S. A missing backend gets zero conformance coverage without any error; three real bugs hid this way. The backend list it needs already exists.

options.label: 2 gen_backlogid BUG (Recommended)
options.description: BUG, effort S. --help writes a tracked file; the rebase check and the 'does this close change the json' output come with it.

options.label: 3 Floor-interpreter parity
options.description: BK, effort S. A 3.11 typecheck in the local fast gate plus fail-fast:false on two CI matrices. Adds some seconds to the gate.

options.label: 4 Session-safety hooks
options.description: BK, effort M. Seven hook changes to .claude/hooks. These bite most often, but the hooks are the hardest to test (real tool calls).

questions.question: Which of bundles 5–8 should get a backlog item?

options.label: 6 Lint traps (Recommended)
options.description: BK, effort S–M. Mostly config and small tests; retires seven gotchas at once.

options.label: 5 Launcher hardening
options.description: BK, effort M. Windows Job Object and a check for the tree changing mid-run; extends run_tests.py.

options.label: 7 Async drift checks
options.description: BK, effort M. A new drift check under DRIFT-RULES.md. Fewer occurrences, but each one cost review rounds.

options.label: 8 Docs build guards
options.description: BK, effort S. Five small guards in the docs-gate; I'd name BK-327 in its orient note.

questions.question: How should the chosen items be filed?

options.label: One item per bundle (Recommended)
options.description: Each bundle gets its own ID and dossier and can ship as its own PR. Matches the PR-scope rule.

options.label: One umbrella item
options.description: A single 'retire memory gotchas' item with a sub-list. Less overhead, but the PR would be broad and hard to review.

options.label: Fold into existing items
options.description: Put 1 into BK-345, 2 into ID-235 and 8 into BK-327; new items only for the rest. Those three items grow in scope.

The evidence narrows bundle 6. What should its item cover?

options.label: Core three (Recommended)
options.description: write_if_changed bytes helper + write_text ban in scripts/ (20 calls, 18 files), ruff PLE2510–2515, hatch {args} with allowlist. Drop the bash/icacls rules (nothing violates them, helper and runbook cover them). conftest stays out.

options.label: Core three + conftest
options.description: Same, plus banning conftest imports. That means migrating the 26 existing imports to plain helper modules first, which makes it an M item.

options.label: Core + all rules
options.description: Everything from the original bundle, bash and icacls as preventive rules with no current violation.

questions.question: The conftest gotcha says 'never import from conftest', but tests/ has 26 such imports. Which side is wrong?

options.label: Memory is wrong (Recommended)
options.description: Repo practice wins: I trim the gotcha to the actual failure (circular/duplicate conftest registration) or delete it if that can't be reproduced.

options.label: Repo is wrong
options.description: Keep the rule; the migration goes into the bundle 6 item (see option above) or its own item.

The trace gate wants a trace for BK-443, BK-444 and BUG-332, but this PR only files them. How should it proceed?

options.label: Proceed without traces (Recommended)
options.description: CLAUDE.md says a trace is owed when the item is worked on, which means implemented or closed; filing isn't working on it. The PR body states why the gate was waived.

options.label: Reword the commit subject
options.description: Amend to a subject without leading IDs (e.g. 'Backlog: file three items from memory gotchas') and force-push, so the gate has nothing to match.

options.label: Stub traces now
options.description: Create three trace files with an orient note each. That's work the CLAUDE.md rule doesn't require, and the traces would sit open until each item is worked.
